podcast.title: Limited Release Demo
podcast.body: Only around 100 copies of the "Demoluca" demo tape were produced, making it a highly sought-after item that occasionally appears on sites like eBay. "There was only a hundred copies made. Well, look at this. From Demoluca, here's Pez, and Happy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording in Parents' Basement
podcast.body: Pez recorded their first four-song demo, "Demoluca," in 1994 in "Johnny's" parents' basement, utilizing a Tascam 4-track recorder. "There was a couple of tapes we recorded first in my parents' basement on Johnny's. He used to have a four track and back then it was a hard thing to find and he had a task in four tracks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Securing First Toronto Gigs
podcast.body: The band gained their first major opportunity in downtown Toronto by providing their "Demoluca" tape to William New, who organized "Elvis Mondays" at the Old Elmucongo. A last-minute cancellation led to their initial booking, which subsequently led to more gigs and networking with other local bands like The Salads and A Flatulite. "Our first big break downtown was we gave this tape to a guy named William New, who had the oldest Mondays at the Old Elmucongo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
